## Before the Lecture: Discover It Yourself

Do these *before* the lecture --- they are designed so that you discover the
concepts yourself, with nothing but a pencil.

- **Six Handshakes to a Stranger** *(handed out in class; the PDF is being rewritten)*: distance, average path length, diameter, and what two long-range friendships do to a village.
- **Do Your Friends Know Each Other?** *(handed out in class; the PDF is being rewritten)*: triangles, clustering, and why any clustering number is meaningless without a random baseline.
- [It's a small world!! 6 degrees of separation](http://estebanmoro.org/pdf/netsci_for_kids/6_degrees_of_separation.pdf) [@esteban-moro-worksheet]

## After the Lecture: Break It

Do this one *after* the lecture --- it takes the same town and pushes it until
the machinery breaks.

- **Turning the Dial** *(handed out in class; the PDF is being rewritten)*: rewiring a ring lattice by hand, deriving how clustering decays with $p$, and finding out that a plain lattice passes the $\sigma > 1$ test.

## Assignments

### Pair Notebook

Work through this module with the AI tutor and hand in the notebook that the session builds. What is graded is your reasoning, not your code — see [the Pair Notebook guide](../course/pair-notebook.qmd) for the setup and a walkthrough of a full session.

- Repository for M02: [`advnetsci-pair-notebook-m02-small-world`](https://github.com/sk-classroom/advnetsci-pair-notebook-m02-small-world). Accept the invitation through Classroom 50; the repository is private to the class.

### Group Mini-Project

Groups of up to three. One repository per group, graded once, with the same score going to every member of the group. Read [how a mini-project runs](../course/mini-project.qmd) first — exactly one person accepts the assignment and invites the rest, and that is the step teams get wrong.

- Repository for M02: [`adv-net-sci-mini-proj-small-world`](https://github.com/sk-classroom/adv-net-sci-mini-proj-small-world). Accept the invitation through Classroom 50 first — the repository is not public, so the link only opens once you are enrolled.

Readers who are not enrolled in SSIE 641 cannot open the assignment repositories. The worksheets above and the [hands-on notebook](02-coding.qmd) cover the same material and need no enrollment.
